Established across two independent implementations in different languages with no shared code: the evaluator, the complete conclusion function (exhaustive distribution 160/49,480/41,820/19,380, identical), and -- as of IND-20260807-3 -- the canonical form and digests, confirmed for the two pinned receipts C11 (703 bytes) and C12 (691 bytes), byte-identical, NOT for all 110,840. committedGates.statement: Register and implement I12 as a hard invariant: conclusion == conclusionFunction(world) AND margin == abs(count(supportingRoots) - count(opposingRoots)). Subsumes I2's and I5's conclusion clauses. COMMITTED GATE (owner direction, RUN-20260807-3 close; evidence base doubled at RUN-20260807-4 per owner instruction). The predecessor committed gate IND-20260807-3 completed and passed; I12 is now the kernel's sole committed gate and the program's exact next falsifiable step, owner's to schedule.
committedGates.evidence: BOTH owner-decision ablations, each corrupting one decision and nothing else, measured over the full 176,120-world enumeration -- by IND-20260807-3 on its side and reproduced on the reference side (RUN-20260807-3 logs/g4-inverted-r1-ablation.txt for R1; RUN-20260807-4 logs/r52-ablation-verification.txt for R5.2): R1 inverted (ties conclude supported) changes 22,440 receipts, R5.2 inverted (margin signed) changes 38,760 receipts; invariant violations detected: 0 and 0, across all thirteen tracked checks, in both implementations; fixtures that catch them: C11+C12 for R1, C12 ALONE for R5.2. The enforcement of both owner decisions is two pinned inputs out of 176,120.
committedGates.exactPassCondition: Under v1.3.0 with I12 registered: the R1-inverting ablation is caught by I12 on exactly 22,440 exhaustive worlds and the R5.2-inverting ablation on exactly 38,760, with no fixture involved; B5 records zero I12 violations; no other number moves.

permanentLimits.note: The two conclusion-function ambiguities the program closed by registered text but never brought to an explicit decision the way R1 and R5.2 were. Recorded per owner instruction at close-out as owner decisions the program did not reach. Both implementations currently follow the registered text; no invariant enforces either reading (the same mechanistic gap as R1/R5.2). Neither is decided here.

A1.question: Does an absence conclusion require at least one supporting root, or is complete coverage alone sufficient?
A1.registeredTextImplies: coverage alone: an absence claim with complete coverage and an EMPTY evidence ledger concludes absent_within_declared_scope (conclusionFunction.absence has no support term)
A1.alternativeReading: absence requires >= 1 supporting root; the empty-ledger worlds conclude not_established
A1.consequence: The 4 affected worlds are the epistemically loudest receipts the schema can emit: bounded absence asserted with no evidence in the ledger at all (the independent implementer's F7/A1, maintained through all three of its runs).
A1.status: owner decision not reached; closed by text without a listed repair (G5); recorded, not decided

A2.question: Does a presence conclusion require complete search coverage?
A2.registeredTextImplies: no: conclusionFunction.presence has no coverage term, so 'supported' is reachable with zero searched locations
A2.alternativeReading: presence also requires search.complete; the affected worlds conclude not_established
A2.consequence: 19,152 of 110,840 receipt-producing worlds (17.3%) change conclusion between the readings -- the largest undecided surface in the kernel. A third implementation reading it the other way would diverge on all of them while passing every invariant (the G5/G4 combination). UNDECIDED: the program records this as an owner decision it did not reach, with both readings preserved. The independent implementer chose the no-coverage reading in IND-1 on the argument that presence is existential; the registered text agrees; neither constitutes a decision of record.
A2.status: owner decision not reached; recorded, not decided
